verification_guide.summary: 5 drugs from 4 mechanistic groups whose current FDA label lists myasthenia gravis in the CONTRAINDICATIONS section: quinine (neuromuscular-blocking antimalarial), diazepam (benzodiazepine), orphenadrine (anticholinergic muscle relaxant), dicyclomine and glycopyrrolate (antimuscarinics). All 5 are returned by PloverDB for the gold query.
sources_used: DailyMed FDA drug labels (current SPL versions, fetched 2026-09-28): QUININE SULFATE capsule (Teva), VALIUM tablet (Waylis), ORPHENADRINE CITRATE ER tablet (Lupin), DICYCLOMINE HYDROCHLORIDE tablet (Hikma), GLYCOPYRROLATE tablet (Par Health)
verification_guide.how_to_verify_a_dailymed_entry: Open the URL (drugInfo.cfm?setid=...). PLR-format labels (quinine, dicyclomine, glycopyrrolate) have a HIGHLIGHTS box and a FULL PRESCRIBING INFORMATION section numbered 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS; older-format labels (VALIUM, orphenadrine) have an unnumbered CONTRAINDICATIONS heading. The per-answer where_on_page gives the position. Quotes with ' ... ' join non-adjacent fragments of the same section. The curator matched every fragment against the drugInfo.cfm HTML and against the SPL XML (DailyMed web services v2, LOINC 34070-3 section) on 2026-09-28.
verification_guide.cross_check_with_ploverdb: Each verified_answer CURIE is in the PloverDB result set for the gold query (n0=MONDO:0009688, n1=biolink:Drug, e0: n1 -contraindicated_in-> n0), revalidated 2026-09-28; supporting_edge_ids are the DrugCentral edges.
verification_guide.intentionally_omitted: Checked and rejected as gold even though they are in the result set: tolterodine (CHEBI:9622): the DETROL label (DailyMed setid 41eb00d2-64e3-4ec9-8732-4bfc81b04180) lists only urinary retention, gastric retention, uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma and hypersensitivity under CONTRAINDICATIONS, and says under PRECAUTIONS "DETROL should be used with caution in patients with myasthenia gravis"; edrophonium (CHEBI:251408): the ENLON label (setid 312042cf-df60-4dc5-90dd-4e77ebd4a781) INDICATES it "for the differential diagnosis of myasthenia gravis" and contraindicates it only for hypersensitivity and mechanical intestinal/urinary obstruction. DrugCentral therefore over-calls some label cautions (and in the edrophonium case a diagnostic use) as contraindications. Other plausible drugs (aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, telithromycin, beta-blockers, neuromuscular blockers) were not label-checked; gold is open-world, so they are not wrong, just unverified. Methscopolamine (scopolamine methobromide, CHEBI:61276) was label-verified (setid 5c74bfb0-c80a-4a86-acd1-1e3a1b20255d) but left out to avoid a third antimuscarinic.

Glycopyrrolate: the KG2c node is CHEBI:90972 'glycopyrronium bromide' (biolink:MolecularMixture per NodeNorm). NameRes rank 1 for 'glycopyrrolate' is a different CURIE, CHEBI:94449 'Glycopyrronium', which is NOT in the result set. A system that answers from the result set will use CHEBI:90972; a system that re-resolves the drug name will not be credited under exact-CURIE scoring.
Diazepam also has a multiomics-drugapprovals 'treats' edge to myasthenia gravis (see alternative_queries_probed). The FDA label contraindicates it; the treats edge is a KG error.
Dicyclomine's label adds that it may be given in myasthenia gravis only to reduce adverse muscarinic effects of an anticholinesterase (5.4); the contraindication itself is unqualified in section 4.
